statement: A client-supplied or wire-level PARTY LABEL (any string identifying one contributor's role inside a multi-party disclosure/computation scope — e.g. a VelaMultiPartyDisclosureScope grant's `party`/`to`, or any structurally analogous label) must NEVER be trusted as proof of who the caller is. Before any system grants a caller a party-scoped VIEW of that party's evidence, it MUST resolve a SERVER-RECORDED, DURABLE binding between (the exact transaction/request scope, that exact party label) and the real, authenticated persona that contributed or was authorized to control that namespace — never accept the label alone, and never accept a binding recorded under a DIFFERENT transaction/request scope even for the correct persona. That binding lookup MUST be anti-enumerating: every non-match case (no binding recorded at all, a binding recorded for a different persona) resolves the IDENTICAL denial shape/message, so a caller can never learn from the response whether the party label exists, whether it belongs to someone else, or whether it was simply scoped to a different transaction. The binding's own uniqueness constraint must be scoped to (transaction scope, party label) ONLY — never additionally unique on the persona — because the same persona may legitimately hold more than one party role within the same transaction, and a broader uniqueness constraint would silently forbid that legitimate case. Once resolved, any further redaction of that party's view must gate visibility of a SHARED DERIVED RESULT on the exact disclosure grant that names this party as the DISCLOSURE RECIPIENT specifically — mere co-computation membership (e.g. a COMPUTE_WITH-class grant) must never by itself be treated as authorization to see a computed/derived output.
classification: The PARTY-GRANULARITY child of CI-2026-09-13-CONSTITUTIONAL-CHAIN-VIEWER-READS-EACH-STEPS-OWN-EVIDENCE-001 (which established that a viewer must derive each STEP's own state strictly from that step's own evidence, never inferring from context) — this candidate applies the identical 'never fabricate certainty, never infer authorization from context' discipline one axis further: it governs WHO may see a given step's evidence in a multi-party setting, not merely whether a step's evidence exists. It is also the read-side counterpart of the identity-binding discipline this same build-order's earlier items established for namespace derivation (services/vela/velaPartyNamespace.ts's deriveVelaPartyNamespaceRef — 'the sender/signer address is never namespace authority') and composition (CI-2026-09-13-MONEYPENNY-COMPOSITION-GATE-BINDS-EVIDENCE-BEFORE-FREEZE-001) — all three refuse to let a cheap, client-controllable label (a signer address, a scope binding, a party label) stand in for a real, server-verified authority relationship.

canaries.assertion: resolvePartyBindingForViewer returns the IDENTICAL { authorized: false } shape whether no binding exists for (requestRef, partyLabel) at all or a binding exists naming a DIFFERENT persona — proven with an explicit Object.keys() check that the denial carries no extra distinguishing field. The two operator-mandated non-spoofability properties are proven verbatim: (1) changing partyLabel=A in the request/query does not make Persona B resolve as Party A even when a real binding for Party A -> Persona A exists on the SAME requestRef; (2) the same persona does not inherit a party binding recorded under a DIFFERENT requestRef. A third case proves the deliberately narrow UNIQUE(request_ref, party_label) constraint is not accidentally undermined by an assumption of 'one binding per persona': the SAME persona bound to two DIFFERENT party labels on the SAME requestRef (two separate rows) resolves correctly for BOTH labels, and a third, unbound label on that same requestRef still denies cleanly. Both recordUnderwritingPartyBinding and resolvePartyBindingForViewer fail closed (never throw) on a missing admin client, a query/write error, or a synchronous exception.

A party that is a COMPUTE_WITH member of a scope, but never named as the `to` of any DISCLOSE_TO grant, never sees the Execute/Quote/Settle steps' real fields (visible:false, fields null, a FIXED generic reason string that never varies with the real disposition/premium/anything else) — including the case where an UNRELATED DISCLOSE_TO grant elsewhere in the same scope names that SAME party as a `party` (discloser) but never as a `to` (recipient) for the grant this test constructs. A party correctly named as a DISCLOSE_TO.to sees the real fields verbatim, with the step's `state` field always the true underlying state (never fabricated as visible or invisible) in both cases. The Authorize step's grants filter (party===label OR to===label) is asserted with exact expected arrays for both the disclosing party and the receiving party in the same scope, including the case the party-view brief itself flagged as a trap: the discloser DOES see its own DISCLOSE_TO grant in its filtered view (it is named as `party`), which must not be assumed away.

The full operator-specified regression scenario end-to-end through the route: party-a and party-b both COMPUTE_WITH a joint request, only party-a is DISCLOSE_TO'd the result; personaA viewing as party-a sees the real Execute/Quote/Settle fields and its own two Authorize grants; personaB viewing as party-b sees redacted Execute/Quote/Settle (real state, fixed generic reason) and its own two Authorize grants (including the DISCLOSE_TO grant it is the discloser on); a party-c with no binding at all denies with a 403 regardless of who is authenticated; the resolved flowOwnerPersonaId is read for the chain-state lookup (never the viewer's own persona) and never appears anywhere in the JSON response body; a full JSON.stringify leak check confirms neither party's redacted view ever contains the other party's real derived-result fields or any raw persona/UUID identifier.

occurrences.defect: A VelaMultiPartyDisclosureScope grant's party label (velaMultiPartyProjection.ts) was a free string with no recorded binding to any real persona anywhere in this codebase — any caller supplying a party label at the route layer would, before this item, have had no gate at all distinguishing 'this caller genuinely IS that party' from 'this caller merely typed that string'.

notes: This is the FIRST recorded occurrence of THIS candidate — status stays `candidate`; only an operator act may raise this to `ratified`/`canonical`.

Parented to CI-2026-09-13-CONSTITUTIONAL-CHAIN-VIEWER-READS-EACH-STEPS-OWN-EVIDENCE-001 per the build brief's own instruction ('this one is its natural child: the same viewer/redaction discipline, applied at party granularity') — a future ratification pass should read both together, and should also cross-reference CI-2026-08-23-PER-AGENT-AUTHORITY-KEY-001 (the general 'a durable store representing a principal's current state must key on [principal, agent/role] — never the principal alone' pattern this candidate's own UNIQUE(request_ref, party_label)-not-persona design directly instantiates, as already noted in velaPartyNamespace.ts's own header) since the two candidates independently converge on the same 'never assume one identity, one role' shape from different directions.

Not yet applied to a second implementation — occurrence count is 1. The natural second occurrence to watch for is any future multi-party surface in this platform that needs to gate a shared/derived result behind a disclosure scope for a specific named party — e.g. a future Reciprocal Artifact Exchange multi-signer view, or a QriptoCENT cross-denomination settlement participant view — which should resolve a persona binding the SAME way rather than trusting a client-supplied role label.
